title: prodRange respects a pointwise identity of its function
statement: Two functions that agree at every natural have the same product over every initial segment. This kernel has no funext, so a pointwise identity cannot be pushed under prodRange by rewriting the function argument; the statement has to be proved by induction on the bound.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.prodRange_congr : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : ((x3 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (x0 x3) (x1 x3))) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.prodRange x0 x2) (AxNat.prodRange x1 x2)))))

evidence.supports: Nat.prodRange_congr is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- prodRange_congr 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -cE '^Nat\.prodRange_congr.7.\(\(x0 : \(\(x0 : AxNat\) -> AxNat\)\) -> \(\(x1 : \(\(x1 : AxNat\) -> AxNat\)\) -> \(\(x2 : AxNat\) -> \(\(x3 : \(\(x3 : AxNat\) -> Eq\.\{1\} AxNat \(x0 x3\) \(x1 x3\)\)\) -> Eq\.\{1\} AxNat \(AxNat\.prodRange x0 x2\) \(AxNat\.prodRange x1 x2\)\)\)\)\)$')" = 1
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted kernel gate, so a successful build IS the type-check. The pattern pins the ARITY and the FULL rendered type, not the theorem's presence: `scripts/new-fact.py` rejected a name-only pattern as population-only, because it catches the row disappearing but not the statement changing inside a row that is still there.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat environment admits no trusted declaration
evidence.notes: Reports `nat: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0 total_trusted=0` over the FULL trusted surface (Axiom, Opaque and Quotient), not `Declaration::Axiom` alone, and exits non-zero unless the surface is empty. The enumeration is per-environment rather than per-theorem; it bounds this theorem's footprint because a proof cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain. Read directly from `Kernel::axiom_footprint` via `theorem_axiom_footprint`, this theorem's row prints footprint size 0 and an empty axiom column, and all 905 `nat` rows do.

provenance.source: theorem name and canonical type read directly via nat_theorem_inventory, which prints render_lean of the admitted type; declared by `nat_prelude/multiset_prod.rs` (lane nat-factorization).

notes: Declared for `Nat.Multiset.prod_add`, which needs to rewrite a fold's FUNCTION and cannot: this kernel has no `funext`, so `count_add` and `pow_add` holding at every point does not let the two lambdas be identified. This is the Nat twin of the already-landed `Int.prodRange_congr`; the Int proof was not transported, because the induction is three lines either way. It says nothing about a hypothesis restricted BELOW the bound -- that would be a `prodRange_congr_lt`, which this lane did not need and did not build.
